author: opt-B1det3

contract.sync_assumed: caller separates consecutive calls that reuse the temp storage by a block barrier
contract.sync_performed: __syncthreads inside: 2 per radix pass plus 1 init, plus 1 in the tie phase when the candidates at the k-th key exceed the remaining k, plus one or two __syncwarp in the warps that hold a candidate
contract.n_range: N = Threads x IPT, IPT 1 to 64 under prefer_smaller_index (the candidate mask is 64 bits per thread), measured 1024, 4096 and 16384 at 256 threads and 32768 at 512 threads. Temp storage 2144 + 8 x warps x IPT bytes: 2400 at IPT 4, 3168 at IPT 16, 6240 at IPT 64, 10368 at 512 threads and IPT 64
contract.type_constraints: fp32 and bf16 through the radix traits, int32 indices derived from the striped tile position
contract.nan_behavior: NaN twiddles to the largest radix key and is selected first, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 is normalized to +0.0 once in the prologue so both zeros form one tie class
contract.tie_break_support: inherent under prefer_smaller_index: per-candidate rank lookup over the exact ties after the last pass. One candidate bit per slot, above 8 items per thread the warp ORs its masks (redux) and ballots only the slots with a candidate into a (warp, slot) table of ballot words, up to 8 every slot, one block barrier, warps with a candidate derive their bases by a shuffle scan (into a base table above 8 items per thread, by one shuffle per slot below), and only the threads with a candidate look their rank up (two shared loads and a popcount) and write out[total_selected + rank]. Index order on striped tiles. The emission ticket of the strictly selected items is one shared atomic per item on a class-indexed counter (T57), on a 32-bit shared address taken once and pinned, the ties draw and drop a ticket on the second counter. Price against B1_idx under not_guaranteed in the same session: bf16 latency plus 4 to 8 percent at N 1024, 10 to 19 at N 4096, 7 to 16 at N 16384, 16 to 24 at N 32768 with 512 threads, fp32 within 2.4 percent at N 1024 and 4096, 1 to 5 at N 16384, 4 to 9 at N 32768, see findings
contract.sorted_output_support: not supported inherently, post-sort of k

low_level: Tie phase SASS, det2 against det3 in one profiler binary (approaches/B1/profile_det3_phases.cu, state/results/opt-B1det3/prof/prof.sass.gz, bf16): at IPT 16 (N 4096 k 64) 283 against 168 instructions, the 16 VOTE.ANY become one VOTE.ANY inside a loop that runs once per slot with a candidate somewhere in the warp (plus one REDUX.OR per mask word), the 16 SHFL.IDX go, POPC 32 against 9, STS 16 against 4 (the row zeroing and the loop store); at IPT 64 (N 16384 k 256) 874 against 402, VOTE 64 against 1, POPC 128 against 18, SHFL.IDX 65 against 0, LDS 16 against 20; at 512 threads and IPT 64 1036 against 484, with det2's 38 STL and 21 LDL gone. The lookup iteration is 24 instructions (FLO on the isolated low bit, two LDS, LOP3, POPC, IADD, ISETP, predicated STS), the scan 136 instructions for two interleaved rounds (16 LDS, 16 POPC, 10 SHFL.UP, 2 STS). Whole primitive 1368 against 1104 instructions at IPT 16, 4248 against 3224 at IPT 64. At IPT 4 the per-slot form costs 173 against 112: the base shuffle per slot and the table load replace det2's register ballot and the any-vote and the skip branch are added.

Registers of the harness latency kernel, det3 against det2 against B1_idx: 40, 40, 32 at IPT 4, 48, 64, 47 to 48 at IPT 16, 128, 206 to 209, 128 at IPT 64, 102, 128 (592 spill bytes, 75 STL and LDL), 100 to 104 at 512 threads. Throughput kernel 32, 48, 127 to 128, 97 to 100 with 8, 5, 2 and 1 blocks per SM, the same as B1_idx (det2 6 to 8, 4, 1, 1). The two per-slot register arrays are gone, one mask word per 32 slots remains. The latency kernel at IPT 16 lands on the 48-register target with 20 (bf16) and 72 (fp32) spill bytes, 3 and 8 STL, all in the kernel prologue and the clock bookkeeping outside the timed chain (run.py flags them, the SASS places them), no spill or stack frame anywhere else. SASS instructions of the latency kernel at bf16 N 4096 k 64 1896 against det2's 2256. Barriers unchanged, 21 (bf16) and 33 (fp32).

The intermediate build (commit 4497544a4f, batches d3) lost 300 to 1100 cycles per call at N 4096 and N 16384 to a rematerialized shared window base: at the 48-register target ptxas recomputed the CTA's shared base (S2UR SR_CgaCtaId, UMOV, ULEA, UIADD3) in front of every ticket atomic because the temp storage is a generic reference, 37 S2UR in the det3 latency kernel at N 4096 against 2 in det2's (64 registers, base kept in UR8). Taking the counters' shared address once with __cvta_generic_to_shared did not help (the conversion was rematerialized), pinning the 32-bit address with asm volatile("" : "+r") and issuing the ticket as atom.relaxed.cta.shared.add.u32 did (6 S2UR). Same control, same node, consecutive sessions: det3 against det2 at bf16 N 4096 k 64 latency plus 2.4 before against minus 4.1 percent after, fp32 N 4096 k 64 plus 6.6 against minus 0.1, fp32 N 16384 k 256 plus 5.7 against minus 2.3. The ticket stays a plain ATOMS, no aggregation.

Phase stamps (T56 method, one block, 32 random normal rows, the last pass stamp to the end stamp behind a barrier on the rows with a tie phase, final commit, node 018, state/results/opt-B1det3/prof/profile_175423.log), det2 against det3 against the not_guaranteed path of the det2 header: bf16 N 1024 k 16 (9 rows, per-slot form) 793, 929, 406, N 1024 k 256 (12) 1175, 1161, 660, N 4096 k 64 (21, sparse) 2508, 1651, 1281, N 4096 k 256 (25) 3066, 2454, 1980, N 16384 k 256 (29) 7445, 5882, 4714, N 32768 k 64 at 512 threads (20) 10425, 4654, 3165. fp32 rows never run the phase, there det3 is 377 to 385 against det2's 421 and the not_guaranteed 453 at N 1024 k 16. By warp 0's stamps at bf16 N 4096 k 64 the sparse ballot half is 291 (det2 524), the scan 402 and the lookup 225 (det2's scan and ranks 722). The sparse form's inner stamps are warp 0's view since the other warps run ahead to the epilogue, the whole-call measure is the one to read.
algorithmic: Same-kernel A/B of the tie phase (det3 against det2, both prefer_smaller_index, same lock section), latency: bf16 minus 0.8, 1.2, 2.0 percent at N 1024 k 16, 64, 256 (1853 against 1868 at k 16), minus 1.6, 4.1, 4.7 at N 4096 (4579 against 4776 at k 64), minus 5.2, 11.0, 14.9 at N 16384 (12941 against 15210 at k 256), minus 10.0, 18.1, 18.9 at N 32768 with 512 threads (16800 against 20535 at k 64). fp32 (no tie at rank k) minus 1.0 to 1.8 at N 1024, plus 1.4 to minus 1.3 at N 4096, minus 2.3 to 4.8 at N 16384, minus 1.0 to 2.0 at N 32768. Throughput: bf16 plus 2.3, 3.0, 4.9 percent at N 1024, plus 9.7, 18.6, 17.4 at N 4096 (541 against 456 at k 64), plus 59, 65, 70 at N 16384 (470 against 276 at k 256, two blocks per SM against one), plus 11, 21, 20 at N 32768 with 512 threads, fp32 within 1 percent at N 1024, plus 4.5 to 5.5 at N 4096, plus 65 to 68 at N 16384 (636 against 379 at k 16), plus 1.6 to 3.5 at N 32768.

Cost model of the per-candidate phase per run: a mask build of about 3.5 instructions per slot (compare, select, LOP3 tree), the row zeroing, one redux per mask word, the warp-uniform ballot loop at about 12 instructions and 60 cycles per slot that holds a candidate in the warp, the block barrier, and in the warps with a candidate the scan (one round about 300 to 400 cycles latency bound, two rounds interleaved about 700 at IPT 64 by warp 0's view) and the lookup (about 150 to 250 cycles per iteration, one or two per thread). On tie rows the deterministic premium over the not_guaranteed path fell from 1227 to 370 cycles at bf16 N 4096 k 64 (minus 70 percent), 1086 to 474 at k 256, 2731 to 1168 at N 16384 k 256 (minus 57), 7260 to 1489 at N 32768 k 64 with 512 threads (minus 79, det2 spilled there). At IPT 4 the per-slot form with the shuffled base and the unrolled lookup costs about what det2's four shuffles and popcounts cost (387 to 523 on tie rows) and the epilogue without the taken branch is 19 cycles cheaper on every row, net minus 1 to 2 percent in the harness.

The remaining price has three terms. The tie phase proper, 370 to 1489 cycles per run on 66 to 91 percent of the bf16 rows at N 4096 and above, now dominated by the mask build and the scan (both per slot) and no longer by anything per tie. The -0.0 normalization, about 450 cycles per call at IPT 64 and 256 threads and 1000 to 1250 at 512 threads on rows without ties (fp32 N 32768 k 16, 12944 against 11914 for the not_guaranteed path), two issue-bound instructions per key at 16 warps per SM. And the register target of the latency kernel at IPT 16 (48 with a few spills outside the chain), which costs nothing measurable after the address pin.

The register saving is the whole throughput story at IPT 64: at 128 registers both det3 and B1_idx run two blocks per SM, det2 at 206 to 227 ran one, so the 74 to 100 percent throughput price of det2 at N 16384 is 5 to 17 percent for det3, and at 512 threads the 592 spill bytes of det2's tie arrays are gone (102 registers, no stack frame).
negative: The warp-sparse ballots do not pay at IPT 4: redux, row zeroing, warp sync and the loop cost 248 cycles against 149 for det2's four ballots in the profile, so the adapter keeps per-slot ballots up to 8 items per thread.

The base table round trip (store, warp sync, load) does not pay at IPT 4 either: 937 against 793 cycles on tie rows in the first build, det2's per-slot base shuffle is nearly free there, so up to 8 items per thread the base comes by one shuffle per slot.

A 64-bit candidate mask walked with __ffsll costs a ten-instruction emulation per iteration (negate, mask, FLO, two subtracts, select) in both loops at IPT 64, the 32-bit halves with __ffs cost three.

Taking the counters' shared address once with __cvta_generic_to_shared did not stop ptxas from recomputing the window base per ticket atomic, the conversion itself was rematerialized, only the pinned register value stopped it.

The fp32 latency price at N 32768 with 512 threads barely moved (8.6, 6.1, 3.9 percent against 9.2, 6.9, 5.0 for det2): there is no tie phase on fp32 rows, the price is the normalization and the det path's code, not the ranks.
surprises: The one-block profile placed the first clock stamp differently for det2 and det3 at IPT 64 with identical prologue source: det3's prologue reads 380 cycles longer because less of the twiddle work is hoisted above the stamp, so the profile totals penalize det3 by that much at IPT 64 while the harness does not. Read the post-pass sum, not the total, when two builds differ in register pressure.

det3 is faster than B1_idx's own not_guaranteed path at fp32 N 1024 (minus 1.3 to 1.9 percent latency) and at fp32 N 4096 k 64 and 256 (minus 0.2 and 1.8), the deterministic variant beats the one it is priced against: the class-branch epilogue is cheaper than idx's bounded tie store by more than the normalization costs there.

The harness latency kernel and the one-block profile disagreed by 800 cycles at bf16 N 4096 k 64 in the intermediate build, and the cause was neither the tie phase nor the 20 to 72 spill bytes (which sit outside the chain) but the rematerialized shared base in the epilogue, a ptxas decision that the register target of the control (64) did not trigger and the variant's (48) did.
open_questions: The mask build (about 230 instructions per thread at IPT 64) and the scan (136) now dominate the tie phase and are per slot, not per tie. Whether the per-slot compare can be shared with the epilogue's own compare, or the ballot phase replaced by something that touches only the candidate slots, is the next lever for bf16 at N 16384 and 32768 (still 12 to 24 percent latency price).

The -0.0 normalization is the largest fp32 term and about half of the bf16 price at 512 threads (1000 to 1250 cycles per call at N 32768 with no tie). Folding it into the first pass's digit extraction (DET_TICKET section 5) is untested.

Whether ptxas can be kept off the 48-register target for the latency kernel at IPT 16, where det2 at 64 registers has no spill, or whether that matters at all once the shared base is pinned (the remaining spills are outside the chain).
The loops run once per candidate slot and per candidate, so flood patterns (all_equal, tie_heavy, quantized_random) cost IPT iterations per thread. They pass the oracle, their time was not measured.
B1_idx's not_guaranteed epilogue could adopt the det3 epilogue spelling (class branch, pinned shared address), det3 beats it by 1 to 2 percent at fp32 N 1024 and 4096 in latency.

correctness_notes: 18 prefer_smaller_index cells at N 1024, 4096 and 16384 (256 threads, label d4a) and 6 at N 32768 with 512 threads (label d4d), variant and control B1_det2 both under prefer_smaller_index, 22 oracle cases per cell including the five signed_zero seeds, signed_zero_boundary and pivot_tie_zero with the exact index check, all passed for both. Control B1_det2 in the same lock section (harness 0.8). The B1_det3 header is a copy of block_topk_b1_det2.cuh in namespace topk_b1_det3 whose functional changes are the tie phase (resolve_ties, ballot_slots, lookup_slots) and the ticket's pinned shared address, the phase stamps compile to nothing without B1_PROFILE. The one-block profiler compared the result digests of det2 and both det3 forms on 32 rows per cell, identical everywhere. The intermediate commit 4497544a4f (batches d3a, d3d) carried the rematerialized shared base of the findings and is not in this card.
